name: Binary Search
description: Efficient search algorithm that finds a target value in a sorted array by repeatedly halving the search space. Compares the target to the middle element and eliminates half the remaining elements each step.
aim: To locate a target value in a sorted array in O(log n) time by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half, leveraging the sorted property to eliminate large portions of the array.
howItWorks: Requires a sorted array as input
Set low = 0 and high = n-1 (the full array range)
Calculate mid = low + (high - low) / 2 to avoid integer overflow
If arr[mid] < target, search the right half: set low = mid + 1
If arr[mid] > target, search the left half: set high = mid - 1
Repeat until low > high (not found) or target is found

time.bestCase: Target is at the middle of the array on the first check
time.averageCase: Target is found after log₂(n) comparisons on average
time.worstCase: Target is at the edge or not present — requires full halving

complexity.spaceDescription: Iterative version uses constant space — no recursion stack

realWorld: Dictionary lookups — searching through alphabetically sorted words
Database indexing — B-trees use binary search on sorted keys
Version control bisect — git bisect uses binary search to find bad commits
Game mechanics — finding optimal difficulty settings or balance points
Network routing — finding IP address ranges in routing tables
whenToUse: Data is sorted (or can be sorted once and searched many times)
Random access to elements is available (arrays, not linked lists)
Need guaranteed O(log n) search time
Searching repeatedly in a static sorted dataset
alternatives: Use Linear Search for unsorted arrays or very small datasets — O(n) but no sorting required
Use Hash Maps for O(1) average lookup when exact match is needed
Use Interpolation Search for uniformly distributed data — can approach O(log log n)
Use a Trie for prefix-based string searching
